The working file is the complete analysis; the reports are its reader copies. Please read one of them in full — this message is only a pointer, not the analysis.

In brief: don't split the file first. To ground this I inspected a real, structurally identical system (this very plugin's own repository) rather than reasoning only in the abstract. Two findings drove the recommendation: (1) in this harness, whether content is "always loaded" depends on *what kind of construct* holds it (an agent body vs. a Read-fetched reference vs. a slash-command-only skill), not on which file a maintainer put it in — so a naive split can leave real cost unchanged while making the line-count gate pass (Goodhart gaming); (2) roughly a fifth of the inspected file's length turned out to be a literally different job (a shell/typst/pandoc document-publishing pipeline), not deepening reasoning method — and the project has already proven, for a sibling concern, that such mechanical content is cheaper and safer as an executable script/hook than as prose. The recommendation (MEDIUM confidence) is: extract that mechanical pipeline into code first, then measure the real generated-artifact token count and redefine the budget around that measurement, then decide any further splitting of the companion-reasoning techniques technique-by-technique against real usage frequency — in that order, with a dated deliverable, so the fix doesn't quietly recreate the original problem (an unenforced, unmeasured budget) one level up.
